observed_result: Master specification section 9.2 (docs/handoff/CoImNet_Implementation_Plan.zh-TW.md lines 408 and 410) fixes the edges 1->2=0.5, 3->2=-0.25, 2->3=0.75 for three neurons, so that input [2,4,8] gives output [0,-1,3], and an upstream gradient [1,2,3] gives weight gradients [4,16,12] and input gradients [1,2.25,-0.5]. internal/sparse/operator_test.go asserts exactly these values at lines 16 (weights), 22 (output), 31 (weight gradients) and 34 (input gradients) in TestForwardAndBackwardHandCalculation, which passed (see the log). The whole-brain run recorded in evidence/NAT-01/verification.json executed 25,563,197 edges with accounted arrays of 24 bytes per edge held twice (simulate/runner.go lines 24-33) plus per-node arrays, measuring 4,378,574,848 bytes maximum resident set size, while a dense 165,122 x 165,122 float64 matrix would need 218,122,199,072 bytes, so no N×N matrix is ever allocated.
assumption_statement: the dense reference in the sparse tests is a small comparison only; the sparse operator is the only path used on the real graph; normalization never overwrites raw contact counts (the raw weight stays in the graph store).
limitations: The touchstone is a fixture; the whole-brain evidence is the NAT-01 run on macOS arm64 only.
No dedicated N×N-allocation guard test exists beyond the accounting refusal test TestBuildRefusesOversizedGraphsInsteadOfDownsizing in simulate/simulate_test.go (line 375).
